name: Space
tagline: The space economy — launch, satellites, earth-observation, comms, plus the defense names riding alongside. Small universe, young funds, heavy concentration, and a big gap between marketing and holdings.
key_tensions: 'Space' vs 'defense' drift: several funds broadened mandates toward defense in 2025 (ARKX literally renamed to add 'Defense'). Pure-space and defense are different risk profiles.
Concentration: funds run ~34-54 holdings with top-10 weights near 50-60% — fairly concentrated bets either way.
Cost: space funds cluster at 0.75%; broad aerospace & defense funds are 0.35-0.50% for more liquidity. Is pure-space access worth the premium?
Data quality: aggregator figures disagreed with SEC filings (e.g. UFO concentration ~58% vs ~22%). Cross-check before deciding.
benchmark_note: XAR and SHLD are aerospace & defense funds, NOT space funds — included as yardsticks. A lot of 'space' exposure is really aerospace/defense; comparing shows how much extra (and how much overlap) a space label actually buys.

cost.note: 0.75% — typical for space, but high vs broad A&D.

purity.note: May'26 holdings genuinely space-pure (Rocket Lab, Planet Labs, Iridium...).

liquidity.note: ~$950M AUM — healthy for a thematic fund.

memo.thesis: The purest passive bet on the space economy: tracks a dedicated space index and, as of 2026, genuinely holds space pure-plays (launch, satellites, comms) rather than filler.
memo.strategy: Passively tracks the S-Network Space Index. Rules-based, transparent, rebalanced per index methodology. No active manager, no derivatives.

purity_verdict.text: By May 2026 the top names (Rocket Lab, Planet Labs, ViaSat, Globalstar, Iridium, Intuitive Machines) are real space pure-plays. NOTE: its 2023 SEC filing showed weaker purity (incl. a furniture retailer, a water-tech firm) — purity is time-varying, re-check at decision time.

memo.concentration: ~50% in top 10 across ~54 names. Moderate for the theme, but the pure-plays are high-beta.
memo.sector_geo: Concentrated in space/satellite + some industrials; international names included. Less defense-prime overlap than ARKX.
memo.cost_context: 0.75% — standard for space, but ~2x the broad A&D funds. The premium buys genuine space purity.
memo.track_record_note: Since 2019. TODO: trailing returns vs a space/A&D benchmark + max drawdown, with dates.
red_flags: ❓ Data: aggregator vs SEC filing concentration disagreed (58% vs 22%) — verify on issuer fact sheet.
❓ Purity changed over time — confirm current holdings.

decision_log.text: Strongest pure-space candidate. Verify current top-10 + concentration on the issuer fact sheet; pull drawdown vs benchmark before acting.

etfs.name: ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF

purity.note: Space AND defense (renamed 2025) — intentionally diluted with defense.

concentration.note: ~59% top-10 in only ~34 names — high single-stock risk.

etfs.overall: Concentrated active space + defense bet — you're buying ARK's judgment.

memo.thesis: An actively managed, high-conviction bet on a handful of space- and (since 2025) defense-innovation companies, picked by ARK. You buy the manager's judgment as much as the theme.
memo.strategy: Actively managed, NO underlying index — ARK selects and re-weights daily. >=80% in equities tied to its theme. Renamed in late 2025 from 'Space Exploration & Innovation' to add 'Defense Innovation', broadening the mandate. Returns ride on ARK's stock selection → key-person/manager risk is first-order.

purity_verdict.text: Recognizably themed (Rocket Lab, L3Harris, Kratos) but the 2025 defense expansion intentionally dilutes 'space purity' with defense + some adjacent industrials (Deere). You're buying ARK's definition of the theme.

memo.concentration: High: ~59% in top 10 across only ~34 names. Combined with active management + volatile theme, expect large drawdowns.
memo.sector_geo: Heavily Industrials (~60%) and Tech (~28%), mostly US. Overlap watch: big defense primes (LHX) also dominate XAR/SHLD — holding ARKX + a defense ETF doubles up.
memo.cost_context: 0.75% top of the cohort, and you pay for active management. Justified only if ARK adds value net of fee.
memo.track_record_note: Active since 2021; ARK funds are famously volatile (big rallies, deep drawdowns). TODO: trailing 1/3/5-yr vs benchmark, with dates.
bull: Active manager can pivot in a young sector
bear: Diluted space purity, overlaps defense ETFs

decision_log.text: Verify AUM + top-10 on ARK fact sheet; pull drawdown + returns vs benchmark; decide whether you want space or space+defense (if latter, compare to SHLD/XAR on cost).

etfs.name: SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF

purity.note: 'Final Frontiers' = space AND deep-sea exploration; broader than pure space.

liquidity.note: ~$200M AUM — thinnest of the space funds.

etfs.overall: Cheap, broad 'frontiers' exposure — but thin and not pure space.

memo.thesis: The cost-conscious, broader 'frontiers' play: tracks an index of space AND deep-sea exploration companies. Cheapest space fund, but the mandate is wider than pure space and liquidity is the thinnest.
memo.strategy: Passively tracks the S&P Kensho Final Frontiers Index (US equities tied to space + deep-sea exploration), tier-weighted. Rules-based, no active manager.

purity_verdict.text: 'Final Frontiers' deliberately spans space AND deep-sea — so it's not a pure space bet. Skews toward Industrials / Aerospace & Defense.

memo.concentration: ~37 holdings; tier-weighted. TODO: confirm top-10 weight from issuer file.
memo.sector_geo: Broad Aerospace & Defense / Industrials, US-focused. Overlaps XAR/SHLD on the defense side.
memo.cost_context: 0.45% — cheapest space option, roughly 40% less than UFO/ARKX. The trade-off is breadth (less pure) and thin AUM.
memo.track_record_note: Since 2018. TODO: trailing returns vs benchmark + drawdown, with dates.
red_flags: 🚩 Thin AUM ~$200M — wider spreads, some closure risk.

decision_log.text: Attractive on cost. Verify top-10 + average spread (thin AUM); confirm whether 'frontiers' breadth fits your thesis before acting.

etfs.name: SPDR S&P Aerospace & Defense ETF

purity.note: Aerospace & defense, NOT space. Benchmark only.

etfs.overall: Benchmark — diversified, cheap aerospace & defense yardstick.

memo.thesis: REFERENCE FUND, NOT SPACE. The broad, cheap, equal-weighted aerospace & defense benchmark. Included to show how much extra (and how much overlap) a space label actually buys versus mainstream A&D.
memo.strategy: Passive, EQUAL-WEIGHTED index of ~41 US aerospace & defense companies; no single stock exceeds ~3.7%. Very diversified within the sector.

purity_verdict.text: No space-specific mandate (some constituents have space divisions). Use purely as a cost/liquidity/diversification yardstick.

holdings_illustrative.name: BWX Technologies / Curtiss-Wright (equal-wt)
holdings_illustrative.note: A&D primes & suppliers, some space exposure

memo.concentration: Equal-weight = very low single-name risk (max ~3.7%). The opposite of ARKX — useful contrast.
memo.sector_geo: Pure aerospace & defense, US. Overlaps the defense sleeves of ARKX/ROKT/SHLD.
memo.cost_context: 0.35% — far cheaper than the space funds, for more diversification and liquidity (but no pure-space upside).
memo.track_record_note: Long history since 2011; the established A&D baseline.

decision_log.text: Yardstick. If your thesis is really 'defense', this cheaper diversified fund may beat a pricey space ETF — answer that before buying space.

etfs.name: Global X Defense Tech ETF
etfs.overall: Benchmark — concentrated defense-tech yardstick, not space.

memo.thesis: REFERENCE FUND, NOT SPACE. A large, fast-growing defense-tech ETF. Included to show the adjacency/overlap: many 'space' funds lean on the same defense primes this fund holds.
memo.strategy: Passive index of defense-technology companies; cap/tier-weighted, concentrated in the big primes (Lockheed, RTX, General Dynamics) plus tech names like Palantir.

purity_verdict.text: Defense-tech mandate, not space. Use as an overlap check: holding SHLD + a space ETF likely double-counts defense primes.

memo.concentration: ~60% in top 10, largest ~8.9%; ~89% industrials, ~60% US. Concentrated in mega-cap defense.
memo.sector_geo: Defense-tech, ~89% industrials, ~60% US. Heavy overlap with ARKX/ROKT/XAR defense sleeves.
memo.cost_context: 0.50% — between the space funds and XAR. Fair for the exposure, but it's defense, not space.
memo.track_record_note: Newer fund riding large 2025-26 inflows on defense spending. Short history.

decision_log.text: Overlap yardstick. Check it against any space fund's holdings to avoid doubling up on defense primes.
